blocks.text: A pie chart is a circular graph divided into sectors, each representing a proportion of the whole. The whole circle is 100%, or 360 degrees, and each sector's angle is proportional to its category's share. Pie charts suit categorical data as parts of a whole, such as types of cells, species distributions or survey responses.

items: Organise the data in a table of categories and frequencies.
Calculate each sector angle: (category value / total) x 360.
Draw a circle and, with a protractor, mark each angle in turn from a starting radius, using different colours.
Label each sector, add a legend if needed and give a descriptive title.

blocks.text: The x-axis is the horizontal line of a graph, usually used for the independent variable; the y-axis shows the dependent variable measured against it. In biology the x-axis often shows time, species or experimental conditions. To make the figure: identify the variables; choose the scale and range; label the axes with units; plot each pair of values; and, where useful, join the points with a line to show the trend.

In the example, enzyme activity was measured at five temperatures: (5 C, 2), (10 C, 4), (20 C, 7), (30 C, 5) and (40 C, 3) micromoles per minute, with temperature on the x-axis and activity on the y-axis.

blocks.alt: Line graph titled The effect of temperature on enzyme activity. X-axis Temperature (degrees C), 0 to 45 in steps of 5; y-axis Enzyme activity (micromol/min), 0 to 8. Orange points at (5, 2), (10, 4), (20, 7), (30, 5) and (40, 3) joined by a light blue line on a grid.
blocks.caption: X-axis data figure showing the effect of temperature on enzyme activity (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).

blocks.text: Error bars on a bar chart show the variability or uncertainty of the data behind each bar, how far the individual values typically lie from the mean shown by the bar. Range error bars run from the smallest to the largest value of a group. Standard deviation error bars extend above and below the mean by one or more standard deviations (mean plus or minus SD). A short horizontal cap is drawn at each end.
